summary.one_liner: A table-driven, incremental JSON decoder written in Python as a fun curiosity, with a recognizer driven by parsing tables and separate action code that builds the JSON structure.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a JSON recognizer that pushes and pops states on a stack, with state transitions taken from parsing tables generated by build_tables.py that match the railroad diagrams on json.org. Each transition triggers an action code (push list, push object, pop and append, push string, push int, push float, handle escapes, and so on) handled by a separate do_action routine, so the same recognizer can produce different output. The driver consumes input one character at a time and can be suspended after any character, building the JSON as it appears. The README also sketches a tutorial for writing the driver in another language, a multi-object stream variant, and a pretty-printing approach (CS-TR-79-770) for encoding, with printer.py and verifier.py mentioned as examples. The author says the project is more a curiosity than a practical replacement for existing JSON libraries.
use_cases: learning how JSON parsers work internally
porting a JSON decoder to another language
incremental parsing of JSON arriving in chunks
parsing JSON with custom number or string handling
verifying a JSON parser that mishandles backslashes or floats
how_to_run: Add the 'states', 'gotos', and 'catcode' lists from json.txt into the same file as the driver, with a comment explaining them.
If json.txt is not in the expected format, write a reformatter rather than editing it by hand.
Implement parse() and parse_ch() driver functions as shown in the README tutorial.
Implement do_action() with the action codes for your desired output structures.
Call parse(input) on a JSON string to get the decoded object.
Optionally run printer.py with a JSON file to parse with verifier.py and pretty print it.
notable: Separates the recognizer (parsing tables) from the action code, so the output format is controlled by do_action
Incremental: can be suspended after any input character and builds the JSON as it appears
Tables generated by build_tables.py that follow the json.org railroad diagrams
Designed to be easy to port to other languages by rewriting only the driver and table format
Includes a pretty-printing approach based on CS-TR-79-770 for encoding
caveats: The author describes it as a fun curiosity rather than a useful tool compared with existing JSON libraries
Requires assembling the driver, do_action, and tables from the README and json.txt; the code is not presented as a packaged library
The README references an encoder example and a float formatter that is not included in printer.py
keywords: port json parser to another language
